script:
Zhao Zhongzheng
The Zhao family was a major clan of the Western Gate. Zhao Zhongzheng was the eldest son of the current clan leader, with a younger brother named Zhao Zhongyang. The Western Gate and Eastern Territory had been enemies for ages, with constant border conflicts. The Eastern Territory had fertile land and was wealthier than the Western Gate, but the Western Gate people were fierce warriors, so neither side could gain a decisive advantage. The highest power on both sides was held by their respective major clans, and the Zhao family naturally occupied a place in the Western Gate's highest echelon. Zhao Zhongzheng had been ambitious since childhood, wanting to end this chaotic era and unify East and West. To achieve this goal, he first needed to obtain the clan leader position.
However, the old clan leader had Zhao Zhongyang as a late-born son and doted on him from childhood, while often scolding Zhao Zhongzheng. Zhao Zhongzheng felt it would be difficult to secure the clan leader position, so through maneuvering, in 1499 he secretly contacted the Li family of the Eastern Territory, trading Western Gate intelligence for resources. This allowed him to rise in business and steadily surpass Zhao Zhongyang, finally improving his status within the family.
Zhao Zhongzheng had a trusted associate named Zhao San, an orphan picked up by the family who had been his childhood playmate. He also planted two people under Zhao Zhongyang: one was Chen Meier, who was to use feminine wiles on Zhao Zhongyang, and whom Zhao Zhongyang loved dearly. The other was Li Cheng, originally Zhao Zhongyang's subordinate, but later his family was captured by Zhao Zhongzheng, forcing him to work for Zhao Zhongzheng.
Only Zhao Zhongzheng knew about these two "spies" and his secret dealings with the Eastern Territory.
One day in June 1507, Zhao Zhongzheng returned to his room to find Zhao Zhongyang there, looking at him in disbelief. Zhao Zhongzheng's heart tightened as Zhao Zhongyang spoke—he had indeed discovered the correspondence about the Eastern Territory dealings. Zhao Zhongzheng hastily tried to explain, but it was useless. Zhao Zhongyang sighed deeply and hurriedly left the room. Zhao Zhongzheng panicked—if this matter was exposed, his life would be in danger. But he knew his brother had been kind-hearted since childhood and probably wouldn't easily harm his own brother, giving him a chance to handle everything.
Zhao Zhongzheng approached Chen Meier to inquire about Zhao Zhongyang's attitude, but Chen Meier said nothing special had happened and Zhao Zhongyang seemed normal recently. Still uneasy, Zhao Zhongzheng decided to strike first and kill Zhao Zhongyang to protect himself.
Zhao San loved money, so by the end of June, Zhao Zhongzheng gave him 200,000 taels in silver notes to kill Zhao Zhongyang, claiming it was to ensure he obtained the clan leader position. But Zhao San was somewhat cowardly—after all, Zhao Zhongyang also held a prominent position. Zhao Zhongzheng had to tempt him further, promising another 1 million taels after the deed was done. He believed that Zhao San, being alone in the world, would eventually do it.
At the same time, Zhao Zhongzheng asked Li Cheng to do the same thing. Li Cheng was extremely reluctant, but with his entire family in Zhao Zhongzheng's hands, he had no choice despite wanting to refuse.
Of course, Zhao Zhongzheng also began his own preparations—after all, he was the most reliable person. The Eastern Territory had advanced technology, so he obtained a mechanical crossbow with a 200-meter range from them—something unavailable in the Western Gate. If Zhao San and Li Cheng failed, he would personally finish off Zhao Zhongyang. After waiting nearly a month, practicing with the crossbow while waiting for the two to act, Zhao Zhongyang remained alive and well. Zhao Zhongzheng couldn't wait any longer—his secret could be exposed at any time—so he decided to act personally.
[July 25th]
That night at 11 PM, Zhao Zhongzheng brought his mechanical crossbow to Zhao Zhongyang's courtyard and climbed the wall to observe. Zhao Zhongyang's room was lit with two figures moving about—one woman's shadow should be Chen Meier. Zhao Zhongzheng carefully aimed at the man. After a while, he heard sounds from the courtyard. It was too dark to see clearly, but he could make out two figures wrestling with each other. He quickly ducked down, afraid of being discovered. After about 10 minutes, the sounds gradually subsided. When he looked again, the figures had disappeared. He re-aimed at Zhao Zhongyang, triggered the mechanism, and shot an arrow. A scream and a woman's cry followed. The woman rushed out—it was indeed Chen Meier: "Help! Someone is trying to assassinate the young master! The young master is injured!" Having failed to kill with one shot and with no second chance, Zhao Zhongzheng had to climb down the wall and quickly leave before the guards arrived. He then casually threw the mechanical crossbow into a nearby courtyard and ran back to his room.
